project.objective: Identify the place of origin in England and the parents of Jonathan Barker (FamilySearch MHGK-WT7), born about 1819 in England, resident in Jasper County, Mississippi by 1850 and Smith County, Mississippi 1860-1880 — distinguishing him from a same-named Jonathan Barker who died earlier.
project.title: Jonathan Barker's English origins

researcher_profile.narration_guidance: One-line preamble per skill invocation explaining what you're about to do. Assume basic GPS vocabulary. Define unusual or specialized terminology inline.

questions.question: What specific town, parish, or county in England do surviving records give as the birthplace of Jonathan ("John") Barker (I1), born about 1819 and living in Smith County, Mississippi in 1880?
questions.rationale: Censuses 1850 and 1880 give only 'England'; the tree's 'London' is unsourced. Parents cannot be identified in English parish registers without a specific locality, so locality is the gatekeeper. Best candidate sources: his death/burial/probate after 1880 (Smith Co., MS), naturalization, passenger arrival, and children's later records (death certificates, obituaries, Find a Grave). Must also separate him from the earlier same-named Jonathan Barker.

stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: c_001 (tree 'London' vs Whitehaven) and c_002 (1870 age outlier) resolved by preponderance.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: LDS register is an original with primary information for baptism/residence and the subject's own knowledge of his parents; christening is primary for parentage at the event (index form).
stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Yes — a specific English town (Whitehaven, Cumberland) and both parents (William Barker and Martha Edwards) are named and corroborated.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Two independent lines: the 1884 Mississippi church register (self-reported) and the 1811/1818 Whitehaven parish entries (clergy-recorded), created by unrelated parties decades apart.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: LDS register viewed as original page image. English christening and marriage are index entries (batches P01280-1 / M01280-1); original Whitehaven register images not yet viewed — recommended follow-up, not a likely overturn.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. Overturning would require a second Jonathan born to a William & Martha Barker at Whitehaven c.1815-1821; the parish batch shows only one. Viewing the original Whitehaven images and checking the 1841 England census would further reduce risk. Find a Grave inaccessible to the agent.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: FamilySearch indexes, catalog and full-text; Church History Library; Find a Grave (attempted, blocked); Ancestry URL handed off. Mississippi state, county and federal record types plus English parish indexes; John/Jonathan/Johnathan variants searched.

items.rationale: Broad indexed sweep for Jonathan/John Barker b. ~1819 England with spouse Elizabeth in Mississippi — surfaces death, burial, marriage, voter, and military entries in one pass and any record giving a specific English locality.

Mississippi, Deaths and Burials 1822-1921 (coll. 2365065) and Find a Grave–derived entries may give his death date/place and possibly birthplace; establishes end of life and separates him from the earlier same-named man.
Mississippi Voter Registration 1871-1967 (coll. 3308840): 1890s registers often record nativity and naturalization details for foreign-born voters.
Naturalization: declaration of intention/petition typically states birthplace, port and date of arrival. Full-text search of Mississippi/Alabama court minutes for Barker naturalization.
Mississippi Probate Records 1781-1930 (coll. 2036959, image-only) — estate of Jonathan/John Barker; may name heirs and occasionally kin in England.
FAN: children Sarah Martha (d.1920), Amanda R Ainsworth (d.1932), Nicy (d.1920) — death certificates and 1900-1920 censuses give father's birthplace; occasionally more specific than 'England'.

items.jurisdiction: US ports (New Orleans, Mobile, New York)
items.rationale: Passenger arrival lists — identify arrival and possibly English origin; low probability of locality detail pre-1850 but may give age/companions.
Find a Grave memorials for Jonathan/John Barker and family — headstones and contributor bios sometimes give birthplace; verify against originals.
items.skip_reason: Find a Grave blocked automated access (bot verification, log_026); site-wide Jonathan search nil (log_025). The LDS register now gives his death (29 Jul 1886, Smith Co.) directly; the researcher may still run the logged URLs manually for a burial place.

log.notes: Top matches: 1880 (John, b.1819 England), 1850 and 1860 censuses (b. England) — all already attached in tree; none give a locality below 'England'. New leads: 1845 Mississippi state census Smith Co. (WD2C-XVN2), BLM tract book entries 1856 and 1891, Confederate CSR entries (1862). Find a Grave Jonathan Barker d. 28 Mar 1863, Vicksburg (QVG2-WD9K) — likely the earlier same-named man the user excludes.

No death/burial entry consistent with an English-born Barker of Smith/Jasper Co. Results are other Barkers (Natchez, Jefferson Co., Union veteran John H. d.1891, etc.). Mississippi had no statewide death registration before 1912, so absence is expected. A 1891 BLM tract entry for Jonathan Barker (62CY-ZFY9) suggests he may have lived past 1880 — needs image check for county.
Father-name search too broad (unrelated John Barker households, school enumerations). No record of Sarah Martha, Amanda, or Nicy surfaced. Next: target children by married names.

Found Amanda P Barker Ainsworth: Find a Grave (QVVY-QZ5K, memorial 27502279; b. 7 Nov 1848, d. 16 Nov 1932, Taylorsville) and 1910 census Taylorsville (MPDG-3ZJ) with husband Asbery S. Index entries do not carry parents' birthplaces; 1910 image would give father's birthplace (country-level only). No Mississippi death certificate index entry surfaced for her 1932 death — derivative only.

Mississippi-filtered FTS returned 0 (FTS coverage of Mississippi court/deed images appears thin or filter syntax mismatch). Unfiltered 1840-1900 query returned 256; first 30 examined — none in Mississippi/Alabama (Washington probate, Massachusetts genealogies, etc.). No naturalization located.

Year filter not honored (20th-century newspapers returned). No relevant hit. FTS not productive for this subject; naturalization item to be pursued via county court minutes (browse images) or external sites.

No marriage record for Jonathan Barker & Elizabeth Turnbow found; results were unrelated English entries. Marriage likely in Alabama c.1844-45 (Sarah Martha b. AL 1846 per 1850 census) — Alabama county marriages not yet targeted.

All 28 index hits are other Barkers (initials J.J., A.J., T.J., born 1850s+; Lafayette, Copiah, Jones Cos.). No John/Jonathan Barker b. ~1819 or any Smith Co. entry. The index is partial; Smith Co. registers (c.1890-92) would need image browsing.

7 hits across four Smith Co. will/chancery volumes; none concern Jonathan/John Barker (Amason will mentions a 'Barker' sawmill; chancery suits name J.G. Barker, James M. Barker, S. Barker; an Iowa judge A.P. Barker). Surviving Smith Co. probate/chancery volumes begin 1893 — earlier estate papers (1880s) appear not to survive on film. Staged ref retained for last volume only; other volumes' hits summarized here.

Jonathan/Johnathan Barker assessed in Smith Co. personal-property rolls 1867 (33SQ-G58D-9R55), 1871 (33S7-958D-9PZC), 1881 Sylvarena precinct (33S7-958D-9GBK), 1883 Sylvarena precinct (33S7-958D-9P9N). 1883 entry = latest record of him alive found so far. Companion search of 1890-95 rolls (004897559) returned 0 Barker hits — suggests death or removal between 1883 and 1890 (OCR miss possible; verify by image).

Zero Barker hits in 1890-95 Smith Co. rolls. Indirect/negative evidence that Jonathan was no longer a Smith Co. taxpayer by 1890 — consistent with death 1883-1890. Needs image check of 'B' pages to rule out OCR failure.
No Barker mentions in either volume.
URL generated; awaiting user capture. No FS-curated Find a Grave search link for Smith Co. — site-wide search used.
URL generated; awaiting user capture. Variant given name 'John' (as in 1880 census).
URL generated; awaiting user capture. Site-wide Ancestry search (records + public member trees). No subscription on file — free account shows member-tree hits; most record images need a subscription.

Bride-side marriage search: no Turnbow–Barker marriage indexed (only an 1835-born Arkansas Elizabeth Turnbow and English Turnbull fuzzy matches). Alabama county marriage books c.1843-45 likely require image browsing; county unknown.

Numerous English-born John/Jonathan Barkers b. 1814-1824 arriving New York 1827-1845 (e.g., Jonathan b.1818 arr. NY 1827; John b.1819 arr. NY 1841). None carries a link to Mississippi/Alabama, and arrival lists of this era give only country. Cannot identify the subject among them without a corroborating detail (companions, occupation, arrival port). No New Orleans/Mobile arrival of an English Barker of right age surfaced in the top 30. Inconclusive.

No duplicate tree profiles for MHGK-WT7. ~30 English Jonathan/John Barker tree persons b.1815-23 exist (Eckington DBY, Norwich, Marston Moretaine BDF, Whitehaven, Colne, Otley, St Albans, etc.) — none carry Mississippi events; cannot be linked without a locality clue. Attached 1870 census (MFSR-DYX) is the same couple (Jonathan b. England + Elizabeth b. AL 1823, Smith Co.) but gives Jonathan's birth as 1811 — CONFLICT with 1850 (1820), 1860 (1821), 1880 (1819). Birth window for English baptism search should be widened to c.1811-1821. Pending record match: 1850 'Johnathan Parker' b. 1817 MS, Jasper Co. (M4LZ-YGH) — different man, should be rejected. Children absent from 1870 entry (married/away).

FAN (wife's family). Tree gives Elizabeth's parents as Robert Franklin Turnbow (b.1793 KY/SC) & Sarah Canterberry; Robert in Rankin Co. 1830, Jones Co. 1840-41, Choctaw Co. 1850, d. Fannin Co. TX 1854. 1850 census Choctaw Co. household of Robert Turnbow (b.1794 SC) & Sarah (b.1800 TN) includes daughter 'Pernetha' b.1836 — same rare name as Barker daughter 'Pernesia A J' (b.~1855), supporting Elizabeth as Robert's daughter. Turnbow households (John, Joseph) also in Smith Co. 1850. Suggests Elizabeth married in Mississippi (Jones/Smith area) c.1844-45, not Alabama.

Only marriage hit: John Barker & Nancy M Blakely, 16 Feb 1840, Itawamba Co. (V2ZP-MNJ) — north Mississippi, different couple. No Barker-Turnbow marriage indexed in Mississippi 1840-48. Jones/Smith/Jasper Co. marriage books of the 1840s would need image check. Also: 1862 Confederate CSR entries (e.g. XFL7-GWC) give b.1813 but no unit/county in index — original on Fold3.

Jones Co. deed hit is a Bryant Barlow (OCR 'Barker') 1861 deed. Tax-roll box hits are Jefferson Co. Barkers (Wm, Abram, L.L., Margaret, John W.) — not Jonathan. No Jones Co. marriage volumes for 1840s found in volume_search; no Barker-Turnbow marriage located.

Jasper Co. abstract of title (Second District, Sec. 33): (1) William Simpson & wife Jane to Jonathan Barker, deed dated 29 Jan 1856, Deed Book 8 p.542 (SW 1/4 of SE 1/4) — matches 1856 BLM tract entry; (2) Johnathan Barker & wife Elizabeth M. Barker to W. G. Suggs, deed c.1858, recorded 8 Mar 1858, Deed Book 9 p.383/389. Confirms wife's name Elizabeth M. and Jasper Co. residence 1856-58, before move to Smith Co. No birthplace/origin. Original deeds (Books 8 & 9) not yet viewed. No marriage record in these volumes.

FAN pivot (English-born neighbours). Jasper Co. 1850: besides the Barkers, only Henry M. Round (b.~1817 Eng.) household with Eliza H. Round (b.~1828 Eng.) and Unity Read (b.~1831 Eng.), and Tho. G. Moore (b.~1810 Eng.) in Henry L. Martin's household. Smith Co. 1860: besides Jonathan, only John Ovendale (b.~1819 Eng.) with John Hoy (b.~1848 Eng.). Tree: Henry M. Round G785-9LY (Jasper Co. 1840-1860, d.1870) — birthplace only 'England'; no Ovendale tree profile found. Neither yields an English locality yet; Round and Ovendale are candidate associates whose origins, if found, could point to Jonathan's. Jasper 1850 staged results not retained (Smith 1860 retained).

John Ovendale: only US record is the 1860 Smith Co. census (b.~1819 England); not found 1850/1870. English Ovendale records of the period cluster in Nottinghamshire (Mansfield, Sutton-in-Ashfield), Sheffield (Yorkshire), Thanet (Kent) and Norfolk — a surname distribution only, NOT evidence for Jonathan. Henry M. Round: Jasper Co. 1840 census, 1845 state census, 1850 census + slave schedule, 1860 census (H M Round b.~1818 England); Eliza H. Round in 1866 state census. Round was in Jasper Co. before Jonathan arrived, so not a fellow traveller in time. No English locality for either man found in FamilySearch indexes. Ovendale staged results not retained; Round retained.

Run directly in browser pane. 9 hits (Headington OXF infant 1822; Maine, NY, IL, OH, TX, WA, GA) — the location filter was not applied as a place restriction and none is a Mississippi burial. No memorial found for the subject under 'Jonathan'.

log.notes: Located Mississippi District record of members 1874-1924 (FHL film 1939, DGS 9071032); FS images return 403 (restricted). Same register digitized publicly by Church History Library as 'Mississippi District general minutes, 1842-1953', LR 3286 11, Volume 1 (1842-1886), asset 4c01c269-2800-4ab8-a0fe-3379e4743be1.

Read in browser pane. Frame 130 (pp.116-119, 'Baptisms' register) entry No.124 (Note: Dead): Johnathan Barker; father William Barker; mother Martha Edwards; born 10 [or 16] May 18-- (year blank), White Haven, Cumberland, Eng.; baptized 21 Sep 1884 Smith Co. Miss. by Thomas Davies; confirmed 21 Sep 1884 Smith Co. by Wm H. Crandall; remarks 'Died July 29th 1886 in Smith Co. Miss.' Frame 134 (pp.124-125) entry No.31: Elizabeth Mariah Barker; father Robert Turnbow; mother Sarah Canterbury; born 18 Dec 1823 Dallas Co., Ala. Frames 45-47 are narrative minutes 1881-82 (missionaries in Smith/Jasper/Scott Cos.) with no Barker mention seen. Name columns of pp.116-132 scanned; no other Barker.

Jonathan Barker chr. 15 May 1818 Whitehaven Town, Cumberland, parents William & Martha (NB73-4NT, batch P01280-1) — matches LDS register. Other William/Martha Jonathan/John Barkers (St Albans 1816, Ipstones, Bradford, Warter, Killamarsh) lack Whitehaven link.

Whitehaven batch P01280-1 christenings with parents William & Martha Barker: Joseph 26 Feb 1812 (b. 24 Feb), Martha 8 Jul 1813, William 1 Sep 1816, Jonathan 15 May 1818, Thomas 6 Oct 1822, Mary 18 Dec 1825, Eliz. 9 Nov 1828 — a probable sibling set (same parents' names, same parish; identity not individually proven). An 1851 England census index entry lists an Elizabeth b.~1829 Whitehaven with a William Barker (not yet examined).
Marriage William Barker & Martha Edwards, 15 Jul 1811, Whitehaven (NKYJ-SY2, batch M01280-1) — confirms mother's maiden name given in LDS register.
Cumbria Parish Registers (3154704) name search returned only fathers named John Barker; Jonathan's 1818 christening not surfaced in this collection by name.

1841 Cumberland census: no Jonathan Barker of the right age in Whitehaven/St Bees. A Jonathan b.1812-16 at Crosthwaite (Keswick) is a different man. Absence consistent with emigration before 1841 (daughter Sarah Martha b. Alabama ~1845), but not proof.
Cumbria Parish Registers, Barker children of a William 1810-1830: none is Jonathan; Whitehaven St James entries not indexed in this collection.

1851 census Cumberland (SGKP-TZB): William Barker, b.~1787 Whitehaven, mariner, widower, with Elizabeth b.~1829 Whitehaven — consistent with father William (Whitehaven baptisms give him as seaman/sailor/mariner) and with Martha dead by 1851; daughter Eliz. chr. 1828.
All England indexed 1818 Jonathan Barker principals: only one christening at Whitehaven (NB73-4NT). Others are in Yorkshire etc. Supports uniqueness.

Batch C/M01280-1 = Chapelry of St James, Whitehaven (parish of St Bees), extracted from bishop's transcripts (films 90680-90681, IGN 7903768, not full-text searchable). H. B. Stout, 'The registers of St. James, Whitehaven: baptisms 1753-1837' is online (film 962101, IGN 7943147).

FTS of Stout transcript (IGN 7943147) for 'Martha Barker' + Jonathan: 5 pages. Transcribed WK3X (pp.126-127): '15th [May 1818] Jonathan of William & Martha Barker. Queen St. Whitehaven Sailor' — verified visually on image. WK8Y (pp.118-119): 1 Sep [1816] William of William & Martha Barker, Queen St., Seaman. WKMT (pp.158-159): 18 Dec 1825 Mary of William & Martha Barker, Queen St., Mariner.

1841 census St Bees (Whitehaven), Queen Street, Marshall Court (M73V-LZR): William Barker 55, Martha Barker 50, Elizabeth Barker 13, all b. Cumberland, in a multi-family dwelling headed by Dorothy Crosthwaite (no relationship column; family structure inferred from surname and ages). Same street as the 1816-1825 baptisms. Jonathan absent. Bishop's transcripts (film 90680) have a gap 1817-1818 per catalog, so the 1818 entry survives only in the original register / Stout transcript.

GRO death index, Whitehaven: Martha Barker 1849 (2J94-NFG) and 1851 (2NX2-595), no ages indexed. Either could be Jonathan's mother (alive 1841; William a widower by 1851 census, taken 30 Mar 1851) or his sister Martha (chr. 1813). Certificates needed to tell them apart.

Birth date/place therefore secondary information from self-report. Year column left blank ('18--'); day reads 10 or 16 — 10 May fits the 15 May 1818 Whitehaven christening, 16 would postdate it.

Record-typing artifact: this is the ADULT LDS baptism of a ~66-year-old convert on 21 Sep 1884, not a birth-era christening. The extraction schema typed the register as 'christening', which makes automated identity checks see a false 66-year birth gap and cap pe_005 at speculative. Substantive identity is confident (see pe_005 rationale, c_001, ps_001).

assertions.value: Jonathan Barker (chr. 1818, son of William & Martha) not listed with William, Martha and Elizabeth Barker at Queen Street, Marshall Court, Whitehaven, in 1841 — consistent with prior emigration to the US.

person_evidence.rationale: 1850 Jasper Co. census household: Jonathan Barker b.~1820 England with Elizabeth and daughters Sarah Martha and Amanda P; consistent with 1860/1870/1880 Smith Co. households and 1856-58 Jasper Co. deeds naming wife Elizabeth M. same_person 0.905.
1860 Smith Co. census: Jonathan Barker b.~1821 England with Elizabeth (b. AL) and the same three daughters incl. rare 'Pernesia'. same_person 0.924.

1870 Smith Co. census: Jonathan Barker b. England with wife Elizabeth b. AL ~1823 — same couple and county as 1860/1880. CONTRADICTION: age 59 implies b.~1811 vs 1819-1821 elsewhere and 1818 christening; capped at speculative pending conflict resolution, though household context strongly supports identity. same_person 0.435.
1880 Raleigh, Smith Co.: John Barker 61 b. England, farmer, wife Elisabeth 56 b. AL. same_person confidence 5.

LDS Mississippi District baptisms register no.124: Johnathan Barker baptized (as an adult convert) 21 Sep 1884 Smith Co., Miss., born White Haven, Cumberland, Eng., remarks 'Died July 29th 1886 in Smith Co. Miss.' Same register no.31: Elizabeth Mariah Barker, b. 18 Dec 1823 Dallas Co., Ala., dau. of Robert Turnbow & Sarah Canterbury — I2's exact birth date and parents. Only English-born Barker in Smith Co. 1860-1880; tax rolls show him to 1883, none 1890-95. Capped at speculative by the tool for two flagged contradictions: (1) tree birthplace 'London' vs record 'White Haven' — the London claim is unsourced on FamilySearch; (2) the 1884 date is an ADULT baptism, not an infant christening, so the '65-year gap' is an artifact of record typing. Substantively this link is strong; upgrade after conflict resolution.

Elizabeth Mariah Barker, b. 18 Dec 1823 Dallas Co., Ala., parents Robert Turnbow & Sarah Canterbury — matches I2 Elizabeth Mariah Turnbow (b. 18 Dec 1823 AL; tree parents Robert Franklin Turnbow & Sarah Canterberry). same_person 0.786.

Christening 15 May 1818 Whitehaven Town, Cumberland, son of William & Martha Barker. Correlates with LDS register (self-reported 1884): born 10 May, White Haven, father William Barker, mother Martha Edwards; parents' marriage William Barker x Martha Edwards, Whitehaven 15 Jul 1811. Fits census birth range; christening 5 days after the stated birth day. Only Jonathan christened to a William & Martha Barker at Whitehaven in the period. Conflict with former tree 'London' resolved in c_001. Probable: index-only christening and a single self-reported bridge record.

conflicts.description: Jonathan Barker's birthplace: tree says 'London, England' (unsourced) vs LDS register 'White Haven, Cumberland, Eng.' (a_132), corroborated by Whitehaven christening (a_116); censuses give only 'England' (a_006).
conflicts.independence_analysis: The LDS register (Mississippi, 1884, informant most likely Jonathan himself) and the Whitehaven Town parish christening (England, 1818, recorded by the officiant) were created ~66 years and an ocean apart by unrelated parties — fully independent. The censuses are independent of both but less specific. The tree's London claim cites no source; no record behind it was found.
conflicts.resolution_rationale: Preponderance of independent evidence (a_132 from src_007; a_116 from src_005; marriage a_128 from src_006) places Jonathan's birth at Whitehaven, Cumberland. The unsourced 'London' entry on the FamilySearch tree is set aside.
conflicts.weighing_analysis: Whitehaven: self-reported specific place + independent contemporaneous parish christening naming the same parents (William & Martha) + parents' Whitehaven marriage (William Barker x Martha Edwards, 1811) supplying the same maiden name. London: no evidence. 'England' in censuses is consistent with Whitehaven.

conflicts.description: Jonathan Barker's birth year: 1870 census age 59 (b.~1811, a_068) vs 1850 age 30 (b.~1820, a_007), 1860 age 39 (b.~1821, a_033), 1880 age 61 (b.~1819, a_086); christening 15 May 1818 (a_116).
conflicts.independence_analysis: Each census was enumerated separately with unknown informants; the christening is an independent English parish record. The 1870 figure stands alone.
conflicts.resolution_rationale: Birth c. 10 May 1818 (christened 15 May 1818, a_116 from src_005), consistent with 1850/1860/1880 censuses (src_001, src_002, src_004). The 1870 age (a_068, src_003) is an error and does not indicate a different man — the 1870 household is the same couple in the same county.
conflicts.weighing_analysis: Three censuses cluster at 1819-1821; the christening (closest to the event, recorded by the officiant) gives 1818. The 1870 age 59 is an isolated outlier (common enumerator/informant error, e.g. 59 for 52). Censuses habitually understate ages slightly; christening 1818 with birth ~10 May 1818 fits all but 1870.
